380: // directive collects tokens until the directive's scope

386: func (p *parser) directive() error {
387: 
388: 	// a segment is a list of tokens associated with this directive
389: 	var segment Segment
390: 
391: 	// the directive itself is appended as a relevant token
392: 	segment = append(segment, p.Token())

394: 	for p.Next() {
395: 		if p.Val() == "{" {
396: 			p.nesting++
397: 			if !p.isNextOnNewLine() && p.Token().wasQuoted == 0 {
398: 				return p.Err("Unexpected next token after '{' on same line")
399: 			}
400: 			if p.isNewLine() {
401: 				return p.Err("Unexpected '{' on a new line; did you mean to place the '{' on the previous line?")
402: 			}
403: 		} else if p.Val() == "{}" {
404: 			if p.isNextOnNewLine() && p.Token().wasQuoted == 0 {
405: 				return p.Err("Unexpected '{}' at end of line")
406: 			}
407: 		} else if p.isNewLine() && p.nesting == 0 {
408: 			p.cursor-- // read too far
409: 			break
410: 		} else if p.Val() == "}" && p.nesting > 0 {
411: 			p.nesting--
412: 		} else if p.Val() == "}" && p.nesting == 0 {
413: 			return p.Err("Unexpected '}' because no matching opening brace")
414: 		} else if p.Val() == "import" && p.isNewLine() {
415: 			if err := p.doImport(p, 1); err != nil {
416: 				return err
417: 			}
418: 			p.cursor-- // cursor is advanced when we continue, so roll back one more
419: 			continue
420: 		}
421: 
422: 		segment = append(segment, p.Token())
423: 	}
424: 
425: 	p.block.Segments = append(p.block.Segments, segment)
426: 
427: 	if p.nesting > 0 {
428: 		return p.EOFErr()

30: // Dispenser is a type that dispenses tokens, similarly to a lexer,
31: // except that it can do so with some notion of structure. An empty
32: // Dispenser is invalid; call NewDispenser to make a proper instance.
33: type Dispenser struct {
34: 	tokens  []Token
35: 	cursor  int
36: 	nesting int
37: }
38: 
39: // NewDispenser returns a Dispenser filled with the given tokens.
40: func NewDispenser(tokens []Token) *Dispenser {
41: 	return &Dispenser{
42: 		tokens: tokens,
43: 		cursor: -1,
44: 	}
45: }
46: 
47: // NewTestDispenser parses input into tokens and creates a new
48: // Dispenser for test purposes only; any errors are fatal.
49: func NewTestDispenser(input string) *Dispenser {
50: 	tokens, err := allTokens("Testfile", []byte(input))
51: 	if err != nil && err != io.EOF {
52: 		log.Fatalf("getting all tokens from input: %v", err)
53: 	}
54: 	return NewDispenser(tokens)
55: }

57: // Next loads the next token. Returns true if a token
58: // was loaded; false otherwise. If false, all tokens
59: // have been consumed.
60: func (d *Dispenser) Next() bool {
61: 	if d.cursor < len(d.tokens)-1 {
62: 		d.cursor++
63: 		return true
64: 	}
65: 	return false
66: }
67: 
68: // Prev moves to the previous token. It does the inverse
69: // of Next(), except this function may decrement the cursor
70: // to -1 so that the next call to Next() points to the
71: // first token; this allows dispensing to "start over". This
72: // method returns true if the cursor ends up pointing to a
73: // valid token.
74: func (d *Dispenser) Prev() bool {
75: 	if d.cursor > -1 {
76: 		d.cursor--
77: 		return d.cursor > -1
78: 	}
79: 	return false
80: }

82: // NextArg loads the next token if it is on the same
83: // line and if it is not a block opening (open curly
84: // brace). Returns true if an argument token was
85: // loaded; false otherwise. If false, all tokens on
86: // the line have been consumed except for potentially
87: // a block opening. It handles imported tokens
88: // correctly.
89: func (d *Dispenser) NextArg() bool {
90: 	if !d.nextOnSameLine() {
91: 		return false
92: 	}
93: 	if d.Val() == "{" {
94: 		// roll back; a block opening is not an argument
95: 		d.cursor--
96: 		return false
97: 	}
98: 	return true
99: }

101: // nextOnSameLine advances the cursor if the next
102: // token is on the same line of the same file.
103: func (d *Dispenser) nextOnSameLine() bool {
104: 	if d.cursor < 0 {
105: 		d.cursor++
106: 		return true
107: 	}

109: 		return false
110: 	}

112: 	next := d.tokens[d.cursor+1]
113: 	if curr.File == next.File && curr.Line+curr.NumLineBreaks() == next.Line {
114: 		d.cursor++
115: 		return true
116: 	}
117: 	return false
118: }

The regression came from commit #5540 ("Track import name instead of modifying filename"), which stopped rewriting a token's `File` when imported — so tokens spliced in from snippets no longer appeared to be "on a new line" relative to their import site (line numbers of snippet tokens are lower than the import site). The nested `import` inside `handle { import responder ... }` therefore failed the `p.isNewLine()` check in `directive()` (caddyconfig/caddyfile/parse.go:414) and was kept as a literal `import` token in the segment, causing "unrecognized directive: import".

Fix (mirrors upstream #5626):
- **caddyconfig/caddyfile/lexer.go**: added `isNextOnNewLine(t1, t2 Token)` which treats tokens from different files *or different import chains* as being on different lines, in addition to the line-number comparison.
- **caddyconfig/caddyfile/dispenser.go**: `nextOnSameLine`, `NextLine`, `isNewLine`, and `isNextOnNewLine` now delegate to that helper; `doImport`'s "first of the line" snippet detection compares `tokensCopy[i-1]` (which carries the updated import chain) via the helper.

Verified: `TestNestedImport` (the exact issue scenario), `TestImportErrorLine`, and all `caddyconfig/...` tests pass; `go vet` is clean.
